英格兰把10%的生物多样性净增益设为开发许可条件,这套法定核算如何运作?又暴露出哪些科学短板?

England has made ten percent biodiversity net gain a condition of planning permission - how does the statutory accounting operate, and which scientific weaknesses has it exposed?

依据《环境法案》,2024年2月起英格兰多数新建项目须使生物多样性较开发前基线提高至少10%,数值由法定栖息地积分体系按生境类型、面积与状况测算,可通过原地改良、异地购地或购买政府信用交付,并以规划义务锁定至少30年管护。批评集中于:积分只度量栖息地外壳而不计物种组成,稀有难替代生境被折价置换,30年承诺远短于群落演替时标且监测经费悬空,净增益恐停留于账面。
Under the Environment Act, most new development in England since February 2024 must leave biodiversity at least ten percent above the pre-development baseline. A statutory habitat metric scores gains by type, extent and condition of habitat, deliverable on site, through off-site land purchases or government credits, with upkeep locked in for at least thirty years. Critics object that the metric prices habitat shells while ignoring species composition, lets rare irreplaceable habitats be traded away cheaply, and rests on thirty-year pledges far shorter than succession timescales, with monitoring funding unresolved - gains that may live mostly on paper.

为什么有学者批评生物多样性补偿是「浮士德式交易」?时间滞后在其中扮演什么角色?

Why do some scholars denounce biodiversity offsetting as a Faustian bargain, and what role does time lag play in that criticism?

因为补偿惯用未来的恢复承诺兑换当下的生境丧失,两者在时间尺度上严重错位。栖息地随开工即刻消失,新建的林地湿地却需数十乃至上百年才逼近参照生态系统,空窗期内物种持续流失,累积成可能永不结清的恢复债;再叠加恢复失败的不确定性与忽视时滞的折算比率,账面平衡实为生态透支。Maron等人据此主张,时滞风险必须计入补偿设计、折算系数与许可审查。
Because offsetting habitually trades present habitat loss for promises of future restoration, two processes wildly out of step in time. Habitat vanishes the day bulldozers arrive, while newly planted woodland or recreated wetland takes decades to centuries to approach a reference ecosystem; through that window species keep disappearing, piling up a restoration debt that may never be settled. Add the genuine odds that restoration fails outright, and exchange ratios that ignore the delay, and balance exists only on paper. Maron and colleagues therefore insist temporal risk enter offset design, ratios and permit review.

生物多样性补偿遵循的「减缓层级」包含哪些步骤?其「无净损失」目标为何在实践中备受质疑?

Which steps make up the mitigation hierarchy that governs biodiversity offsetting, and why is its no-net-loss goal widely challenged in practice?

依次为避免、最小化、恢复、补偿四个层级。项目应先在选址设计阶段避开敏感栖息地,再压缩影响的范围与强度,对受损地实施原位生态恢复,最后才用保护或重建等效生境抵消剩余损失,力求开发后生物多样性「无净损失」乃至净增益。质疑集中在三点:物种组成与生态功能难以一对一等价替换,生态恢复常有数十年滞后且可能失败,基线与折算方法易被高估操纵,故学界坚持补偿只能是最后手段,不应沦为付费破坏的许可证。
Avoid, minimise, restore, offset - strictly in that order. A project should first be sited away from sensitive habitat, then shrink the scale and intensity of remaining impacts, repair damaged areas in place, and only at the end compensate residual losses by protecting or recreating equivalent habitat, aiming for no net loss - ideally net gain - of biodiversity. The scepticism rests on three points: species composition and ecological function rarely substitute one-for-one, restoration often lags for decades and can fail outright, and baselines and exchange ratios invite optimistic accounting, so researchers insist offsets remain a last resort, not a licence to pay and destroy.

美国的湿地「补偿银行」是怎样运作的?开发商为何要购买它的生态信用?

How does a wetland mitigation bank in the United States work, and why do developers buy its ecological credits?

一种先修复、后开发的信用交易机制。银行发起人先行恢复或新建整片湿地,经跨机构评审团队验收后按功能面积折算成信用单位出售;依《清洁水法》第404条,开发商对无法避免的湿地损失须购得足够信用方可取得许可,兑换比例通常高于一比一。相比项目方各自零散补救,银行在流域尺度上提前集中修复,生态完整性更好,长期维护责任也更明确。
A restore-first, sell-later credit system. A bank sponsor restores or creates a consolidated wetland parcel ahead of any impact; once an interagency review team certifies the site, its functional acreage is converted into sellable credits. Under Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, a developer whose project unavoidably damages wetlands must secure enough credits before a permit issues, usually at ratios above one-to-one. Concentrated, completed-in-advance restoration at watershed scale delivers better ecological coherence and clearer long-term stewardship than piecemeal fixes.
